primary_secondary.note: Own conceptual model with own expert and student validation.

study_type.claude: Other (conceptual model proposal with expert-judgment and exploratory validation)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (conceptual modelling, expert judgment, exploratory Scrum workshops/surveys, iterative review)
study_type.note: Claude frames the design as a conceptual model proposal (-> Other); NotebookLM labels it Mixed methods.

research_method.claude: Conceptual model (UML class diagram) following the Fenton & Bieman protocol in two phases (design, validation); expert judgment (Likert 1-5, mean/SD), exploratory empirical validation (workshops + survey in academic setting), iterative review; comparison with four literature models on criteria C1-C9
research_method.nlm: Conceptual modelling (UML) based on Fenton & Bieman protocol; content validation by expert judgment (Likert); exploratory empirical application via Scrum workshops/surveys; iterative review; comparative scoring against SPACE, DAT, MCRT, SHF on 9 criteria
research_method.value: Conceptual model proposal (UML class diagram) following the Fenton & Bieman measurement protocol in two phases (design, validation); content validation by expert judgment (10 experts, five-point Likert, mean/SD), exploratory application in Scrum workshops with 110 students plus acceptance survey, iterative review; author-scored comparison with four existing models (SPACE, DAT, MCRT, SHF) on nine criteria
research_method.note: No productivity values measured; validation is perception-based.

context.claude: academic; experts with MinCiencias researcher classification; 110 final-semester students at four Colombian HEIs in Scrum teams, two three-week sprints, 2024-2025
context.nlm: academic; 4 Colombian HEIs, 110 undergraduate Systems/Software Engineering students, 10 MinCiencias-recognized experts; 2 sprints (6 weeks)
context.value: academic; four Colombian higher education institutions, student Scrum teams over two sprints (six weeks); 10 experts (content validation) and 110 undergraduate Systems/Software Engineering students (exploratory validation)
context.note: Number of student teams not reported.

cat_productivity.note: Velocity (sum of user stories completed per iteration), work capacity and team capacity among model factors.

cat_quality.note: Quality is a model factor (Flexibility category); participants suggested rework and post-delivery errors.

cat_collaboration.note: Communication factor (Socio Human); participants asked for collaboration/communication evaluation.

cat_satisfaction.note: Team satisfaction, customer satisfaction, intrinsic motivation, pride, commitment among model factors.

cat_activity.note: Borderline: DAT, MCRT (code contributions) and SPACE Activity only described in background and compared in Table 5; not used.

cat_delivery.note: No deployment, lead-time or cycle-time metric.

cat_devex.note: NotebookLM tags several socio-human factors as DevEx, but the DevEx framework is not used.

cat_agile.note: Measurement process operationalized for Scrum (BPMN; planning, execution, evaluation); velocity per iteration.

cat_survey.note: Expert Likert instrument and acceptance survey with students.

evidence.quote: The development of the model was based on the measurement protocol proposed by Fenton and Bieman and included two main stages: design and validation.
The validation was conducted in an academic setting involving 110 university students enrolled in Software Engineering courses at four Higher Education Institutions in Colombia.
The duration of the study was six weeks, structured into two sprints
